questions.stem: Which of the following highly common gases is the major anthropogenic (human-caused) contributor to the enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming?

options.option_text: Nitrogen gas (N₂)
Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
Oxygen gas (O₂) (alternative interpretation)
Argon gas (Ar) (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: While water vapor is the most abundant natural greenhouse gas, carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the burning of fossil fuels and deforestation is the primary driver of human-induced climate change.

questions.stem: The protective ozone layer, which strictly absorbs extremely harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, is located in which specific layer of the atmosphere?

options.option_text: Troposphere
Mesosphere
Stratosphere
Thermosphere

questions.explanation: About 90% of atmospheric ozone is found in the stratosphere (between 10 km and 50 km altitude). This 'good ozone' shields the Earth. Ozone in the troposphere (ground level) is a harmful pollutant.

questions.stem: Which specific highly toxic chemical compound was tragically leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant during the devastating 1984 Bhopal Gas Tragedy?

options.option_text: Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN)
Methyl Isocyanate (MIC)
Phosgene Gas (COCl2)
Ammonium Nitrate (NH4NO3)

questions.explanation: The Bhopal gas tragedy (Dec 1984) is considered one of the world's worst industrial disasters. It was caused by the accidental release of over 40 tons of highly toxic Methyl Isocyanate (MIC) gas, which was used in manufacturing pesticides.
